nodes.label: AeroSpace Project Values
nodes.rationale: Targeted at advanced users; keyboard centric; no GUI for configuration; practical features over ricing; dark magic (private APIs, code injection) avoided — only _AXUIElementGetWindow is used and SIP never needs disabling; goal is maintainability and resistance to macOS updates. Non-values: playing nicely with macOS Spaces, and ricing.

nodes.label: OpenSpec Store Selection
nodes.rationale: --store <id> is sticky for a whole workflow so every spec/change read and write targets the same registered store; without a store, commands act on the nearest local openspec/ root.

nodes.label: Inline Sync Before Archive
nodes.rationale: Archive must run the delta-spec sync inline and re-verify every capability's main spec before moving changeRoot: a background sync would have changeRoot moved out from under it, leaving the change archived while main specs were never updated. On any mismatch the archive stops with changeRoot intact so the sync can be retried.

nodes.label: Explore Mode Stance
nodes.rationale: Explore mode is a stance, not a workflow: no fixed steps, no mandatory outputs. It is for thinking, not implementing - creating OpenSpec artifacts is capturing thinking, while writing application code is forbidden until the user exits explore mode and starts a change.

nodes.label: Artifact Dependency Graph
nodes.rationale: openspec status is file-existence only, so a done artifact does not prove its dependencies exist; the required set is built by walking requires edges transitively from applyRequires, and dependencies are enablers, not gates - a blocked artifact whose only missing dependency was deliberately skipped is still created.

nodes.label: Planning Boundary Principle
nodes.rationale: The request that triggers the propose workflow authorizes planning only, even if it asks to build or fix something; implementation must wait for a new explicit user request, preventing scope creep from plan into code within one response.

nodes.label: Capability Retirement Rules
nodes.rationale: A spec whose last requirement is removed is deleted rather than left with an empty Requirements section, but only when six conditions hold, including the change's .openspec.yaml declaring retire_capabilities: true and the spec.md resolving inside the real specs root (symlink guard against deleting external files).

nodes.label: Intelligent Merging Principle
nodes.rationale: Agent-driven merging is chosen over programmatic overwrite so a scenario can be added without copying the entire requirement; anything the delta does not mention is preserved in the main spec's existing order, and the operation must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Bundled Dependencies License Index
nodes.rationale: legal/README.md indexes the bundled third-party licenses and correctly omitted the orphaned tomlplusplus entry throughout. After #3 the legal/third-party-license/ directory holds exactly four files: LICENSE-HotKey.txt, LICENSE-ISSoundAdditions.txt, LICENSE-TOMLDecoder.txt and LICENSE-swift-collections.txt, so index and directory now agree.

nodes.label: tomlplusplus License File (deleted in #3)
nodes.rationale: RESOLVED / CLOSED per the 2026-08-20 errata. The orphaned license file was deleted by PR #3 (a6f9167b), carrying out the memo's recommendation. tomlplusplus was never a dependency on any axis -- Package.swift:24-29 and Package.resolved pin only HotKey, TOMLDecoder 0.4.4, swift-collections and ISSoundAdditions, and TOMLDecoder is pure Swift. The file was an upstream oversight: added 2024-07-07 (2d21f579) in the TOMLKit era when TOMLKit wrapped the tomlplusplus C++ library, and missed when 16a0b634 (Migrate from TOMLKit to TOMLDecoder, 2026-03-27) removed the README entries and deleted LICENSE-TOMLKIT.txt. The memo's 'repo-wide grep matches only the license file itself' claim no longer holds in either direction: the file is gone and #3 added three prose mentions in dev-docs/fork-maintenance.md (lines 79, 82, 112) recording the deletion as a deliberate fork delta.

nodes.label: TOMLKit to TOMLDecoder Migration
nodes.rationale: Commit 16a0b634 (2026-03-27) replaced TOMLKit -- a Swift wrapper over the tomlplusplus C++ library -- with the pure-Swift TOMLDecoder 0.4.4, eliminating the transitive C++ dependency. The migration cleaned up the README entries and LICENSE-TOMLKIT.txt but left LICENSE-tomlplusplus.txt behind; that residue was finally cleared by fork PR #3.

nodes.label: Common Shared SPM Library Target
nodes.rationale: Common is not a file but the shared SPM library target declared at Package.swift:39-45, and it is the ONLY in-repo target that both Cli (Package.swift:68) and AppBundle (Package.swift:53) depend on. Its 57-community fan-out is composed entirely of AST 'import Common' edges. Per the 2026-08-20 errata the edge count is superseded: #6 added Sources/AppBundleTests/CompletionGrammarTest.swift with '@testable import Common' on line 2, bringing test files to 46 (not 45) and the total to 159 import edges (not 158), so the memo's 'grep count matches exactly' parenthetical no longer holds. AppBundle (111) and Cli (2) are unchanged.

nodes.label: Import-Graph Bridge Artifact (Betweenness Inflation)
nodes.rationale: The bridge SHAPE is an artifact of granularity mismatch: one coarse module node sits against 58 fine-grained file-level communities, inflating betweenness to 0.116. The shape is misleading but the fan-in it exaggerates is genuine, so the metric should be read as a modelling artifact rather than a coupling smell.

nodes.label: Shared-Parser Constraint (Client Parse, Server Re-Parse)
nodes.rationale: Args are parsed on the client (Sources/Cli/_main.swift:58) for --help and early-exit shortcuts, sent over the Unix socket, then re-parsed on the server (server.swift:71 -> parseCommand.swift:26) using the same code. Because both sides must link the identical parser, the arg structs have to live in Sources/Common/cmdArgs/ -- this is the real architectural reason for Common's enormous fan-in, distinct from the graph-shape artifact.

nodes.label: assertEquals Edge-Correctness Verdict
nodes.rationale: Exhaustively verified rather than sampled: all INFERRED edges are calls edges from distinct test methods across 39 files under Sources/AppBundleTests/, with correct caller->callee direction, resolving to the sole repo-wide declaration at assert.swift:34. The 2026-08-20 errata supersedes the caller count -- there are now 283 distinct test methods, not 281, after #5 added testDeprecatedAliasIsValidatedLikeTheCanonicalName() and #6 added testNotHelpDoesNotLeakTestUsage(), both in files that already had callers. The correctness verdict itself is unaffected.

nodes.label: Cross-File INFERRED Downgrade (Swift Module-Scoped Visibility)
nodes.rationale: Swift visibility is module-scoped, so a cross-file call inside one module carries no import statement to serve as evidence. The extractor therefore conservatively downgrades cross-file name resolution to INFERRED, while the 10 intra-assert.swift edges stay EXTRACTED. The INFERRED label reflects extractor conservatism, not uncertainty about correctness.

nodes.label: parseCommand Raw Call-Site Count (superseded: 334, not 331)
nodes.rationale: Superseded by the 2026-08-20 errata. PRs #5/#6 added three single-argument parseCommand( call sites (MoveWorkspaceToMonitorCommandTest.swift:16 and :17, TestCommandTest.swift:37), so the memo's own counting model now yields 334 raw call sites, not the 331 stated in the Answer prose.

nodes.label: Per-Calling-Function Call-Edge Dedup Rule
nodes.rationale: The graph emits exactly one call edge per calling function rather than one per raw call site, collapsing 331 raw sites into 221 edges in the snapshot. Per the 2026-08-20 errata this dedup rule still holds unchanged after the re-map to be847df0; only the raw-site count moved.

nodes.label: parseCommand Node Disambiguation (Test Helper vs Production)
nodes.rationale: The feared test/production conflation did NOT happen: the 220-edge node is the TEST helper parseCommand (Sources/AppBundleTests/testUtil.swift:101), while the production overloads (Sources/AppBundle/command/parseCommand.swift:3 and :25) form a separate degree-13 node. Swift overload resolution is what makes the attribution safe -- every test call site is a single-String call that can only resolve to the helper. 12/12 sampled edges verified, correct direction. One harmless merge remains (the two production overloads share one node) and two recall gaps exist (helper-to-production delegation and the production recursive call have no edges) -- these are missing edges, not wrong edges.
nodes.norm_label: parsecommand node disambiguation (test helper vs production)

nodes.label: MacApp + RunLoopJob Concurrency Backbone
nodes.rationale: MacApp paired with RunLoopJob (MacApp.swift:74, 152, 182, 355; runLoop.swift:61, 74) is the strict-concurrency backbone: every Accessibility API access is dispatched as a cross-thread job rather than called inline. This is what lets the project satisfy Swift strict concurrency while talking to a fundamentally synchronous, thread-affine AX API.

nodes.label: Config Parsing Depends on CLI Arg Grammar
nodes.rationale: parseConfig.swift:186 and :192 call parseCommand, so the config file's validity is defined by the CLI argument grammar. The consequence is non-obvious and load-bearing: an upstream change to command arg parsing silently changes which user config files are accepted, with no separate config-schema versioning to catch it.
nodes.norm_label: config parsing depends on cli arg grammar

nodes.label: KnownBundleId Window Classification Table
nodes.rationale: Window classification is not a general algorithm but a 30-case per-app bundle-ID lookup table: KnownBundleId.swift, consulted from AxUiElementWindowType.swift at lines 21, 101, 172 and 202. Behavior is therefore app-specific by construction, and adding support for an app means extending the table rather than generalizing a rule.

nodes.label: Shell Command Front-End (runShellOr/And/Seq/Pipe)
nodes.rationale: Shell.swift:121-160 defines runShellOr, runShellAnd, runShellSeq and runShellPipe -- an alternate front-end that drives command execution with pipefail semantics, parallel to the socket/CLI path. It is a second entry point into the command pipeline that import-level analysis does not surface.

nodes.label: Subsystem Coupling Map (Beyond Imports)
nodes.rationale: Verified exploration with no refutations. The numerically dominant non-import couplings are test plumbing (parseCommand, .new(), assert helpers at 112+52+51+49 edges) and should be filtered out before reading the map; the real architectural signals are the mouse subsystem's structural anonymity, the focus/config command cycle, config's dependence on the CLI grammar, the shell front-end, the bundle-ID classification table, and the MacApp+RunLoopJob concurrency backbone.

nodes.label: onFocusChanged Recursion Guard
nodes.rationale: Focus events execute user-configured command shells via config.onFocusChanged.run, creating a config->focus->command->focus cycle that is broken only by a single global boolean, onFocusChangedRecursionGuard (focus.swift:119, 143-145). Per the 2026-08-20 errata the call-site citation is corrected: config.onFocusChanged.run is at Sources/AppBundle/focus.swift:170, not :171 -- line 171 is the closing brace of onFocusChanged(_:_:_:), which spans 165-171. focus.swift is byte-identical between d42555f6 and be847df0, and the two companion citations in the same sentence are exact.

nodes.label: Mouse Subsystem Structural Anonymity
nodes.rationale: mouse/ owns no types of its own: resizeWithMouse.swift:81-96 defines a fileprivate extension ON TreeNode that mutates weights via userData, and moveWithMouse.swift:52 nulls window.lastAppliedLayoutPhysicalRect. Both reach across into tree state and both invalidate the lock-screen closedWindowsCache, so the subsystem is invisible to type-level analysis while being deeply coupled. Both entry paths carry an upstream 'todo cover with tests' marker.

CLAUDE.md previously named a type MacosUnconventionalWindowsContainer that does not exist -- the file defines four separate sibling container classes -- and placed normalizeLayoutReason.swift under tree/ when it lives one level up at Sources/AppBundle/. #4 (95a4f91f) rewrote CLAUDE.md:180-187 to state that the file declares no type of that name, list the four containers, and correct the path.

nodes.label: move-workspace-to-display Validation Bypass (fixed in #5)
nodes.rationale: CLOSED per the 2026-08-20 errata. The deprecated alias move-workspace-to-display had been registered with the raw MoveWorkspaceToMonitorCmdArgs.init (cmdArgsManifest.swift:124) instead of parseWorkspaceToMonitorCmdArgs (:122), so it silently accepted --wrap-around combined with a monitor-pattern that the primary command rejects via the filter at MoveWorkspaceToMonitorCmdArgs.swift:21-26. #5 registers parseWorkspaceToMonitorCmdArgs at :124 and demotes the init to fileprivate, making the bypass structurally impossible rather than merely corrected, with a regression test at MoveWorkspaceToMonitorCommandTest.swift:14-18.

nodes.label: Command Pipeline Four-Place Consistency
nodes.rationale: At the command-SET level the four places agree exactly: 45 CmdKind cases = 45 toCommand() entries = 45 docs adoc files, with the grammar holding 44 because exec-and-forget is legitimately exempt. All FLAG-level discrepancies found by this memo are CLOSED as of the 2026-08-20 errata. Graph note that still stands: the CmdKind cases 'close' and 'split' were mis-clustered into unrelated communities because their labels are generic English words.

nodes.label: exec-and-forget Grammar Exemption
nodes.rationale: The BNF grammar lists 44 commands against 45 CmdKind cases, and the gap is deliberate rather than drift: exec-and-forget is config-only, never invokable from the CLI, and toCommand() hard-fails it at cmdManifest.swift:27-28. Any consistency checker over the four places must special-case it or it will report a false positive.

nodes.label: BNF Grammar Flag Rot (all five fixed in #5)
nodes.rationale: CLOSED per the 2026-08-20 errata -- do not act on these. All five flag-level divergences in grammar/commands-bnf-grammar.txt were fixed in #5 (4e7a7a59): (1) echo advertised --window while the parser accepts only --window-id, now ':24' reads 'echo [--stderr|--window-id <window_id>]... -- <string>...' (the companion citation EchoCmdArgs.swift:10 was always off by one; the flag is at :9); (2) move-workspace-to-monitor --workspace added at :76-78, not the cited 71-72; (3) reload-config --warnings-as-errors added at :80, not 74; (4) subscribe exclusivity split into two productions at :126-127, not 118, with the parser citation SubscribeCmdArgs.swift:23-28 still exact; (5) the mandatory 'eval <aerospace_shell_expr>' positional restored at :30 with the terminal at :136.

nodes.label: CompletionGrammarTest Drift Guard
nodes.rationale: Added by #6 at Sources/AppBundleTests/CompletionGrammarTest.swift to prevent the flag-level grammar rot from recurring. Because the hand-maintained BNF grammar feeds shell-completion generation but is not derived from the parser, only an executable test can keep the two in sync -- documentation alone had already failed to.

nodes.label: Fork No-Delta Policy Amendment
nodes.rationale: The memo's closing clause 'fix belongs upstream per fork no-delta policy' is superseded. #5/#6 fixed the CLI grammar and alias-validation defects locally, and the policy was amended to match, so the fork now deliberately carries a small set of upstream CLI bug fixes -- recorded at FORK.md:8 and :23 and CLAUDE.md:10-11. The trade-off accepted is a permanent rebase conflict surface in exchange for a working CLI.

nodes.label: Deliberate Out-of-Session Mutations
nodes.rationale: Two mutations sit outside any session and both are currently safe. (1) The startup bootstrap at initAppBundle.swift:22-23 runs garbageCollectUnusedWorkspaces and focusWorkspace after the server and observers are live at :20-21 -- safe ONLY because that stretch is synchronous @MainActor; inserting an await would break it, making this a latent fragility rather than a settled design. (2) resetManipulatedWithMouseIfPossible on mouse-up (GlobalObserver.swift:57-62) mutates only non-structural bookkeeping. The termination path (appBundleUtil.swift:28-52) also bypasses sessions but never mutates the tree, and its comment forbids .parent calls.

nodes.label: Refresh-Session Invariant
nodes.rationale: VERIFIED and re-checked against be847df0: every tree-structure mutation outside Sources/AppBundle/tree/ traces back to a refresh session. The invariant exists so that the on-focus-changed and broadcast machinery stays consistent -- any new code path that mutates the tree must route through runLightSession or refreshModel. Note the 2026-08-20 errata: the memo's 'graph in-edges match grep 1:1' parenthetical does not hold, because the count was wrong when written; the invariant itself survives unchanged.

nodes.label: Single-Flight activeRefreshTask Slot
nodes.rationale: One @MainActor task slot activeRefreshTask (refresh.swift:5) enforces single-flight: scheduleCancellableCompleteRefreshSession cancels the prior task (:12) and re-checks cancellation on entry (:14); runLightSession preempts the heavy session (:66-67) and reschedules one at exit (:86). Light sessions are deliberately NOT slot-registered, so light-light interleaving at await points remains possible -- that residual hazard is mitigated by calling refreshModel immediately before and after the command body (:74-76) rather than by a second lock.

nodes.label: runLightSession Call-Site Count (corrected: 13, not 12)
nodes.rationale: Superseded by the 2026-08-20 errata, and notably the count was already wrong when the memo was written rather than being invalidated by PRs #3-#6. There are 13 runLightSession call sites (excluding the declaration at layout/refresh.swift:59): GlobalObserver.swift:26 and :68, initAppBundle.swift:31, server.swift:90, ui/MenuBar.swift:19, :34, :54, :116, config/ConfigFileWatcher.swift:39, config/HotkeyBinding.swift:39, mouse/moveWithMouse.swift:19, mouse/resizeWithMouse.swift:19, mouse/focusFollowsMouse.swift:46.

nodes.label: CmdArgs Conformance Table (45 conformers)
nodes.rationale: Flat protocol conformance table at the CLI boundary: 45 CmdArgs conformers against the protocol declared at Sources/Common/cmdArgs/parseCmdArgs.swift:13, wired through the cmdArgsManifest switch.

nodes.label: CmdArgs Node Fragmentation (patched; recurs after --force)
nodes.rationale: FIXED per the 2026-08-20 errata, but only as a data patch. Previously all 45 implements edges targeted a placeholder node id 'cmdargs' with no source_file while 8 other CmdArgs-labeled nodes existed and the real declaration node received zero implements edges. Today there is no node with id 'cmdargs'; the single CmdArgs node is the real declaration at Sources/Common/cmdArgs/parseCmdArgs.swift:13 and it receives all 45 implements edges. The extractor still re-mints the placeholder whenever a *CmdArgs.swift file is re-extracted, and the merge had to be re-applied during the 2026-08-20 re-map -- expect the fragmentation again after any 'graphify extract --force'.

nodes.label: Command Conformance Table (44 conformers)
nodes.rationale: The server-side twin of the CmdArgs table: 44 Command conformers wired by the toCommand() manifest switch. It is one short of the 45 CmdArgs conformers because exec-and-forget is config-only and has no server-side command.

nodes.label: implements-Edge Semantic Conflation
nodes.rationale: The implements relation conflates two unrelated Swift constructs: raw-value enum backing (enum X: String contributes 18 edges pointing at String) and genuine protocol conformance. Method edges suffer a parallel conflation between call sites and extension definitions -- LexerToken's external methods are all test invocations, not definitions. Consumers reasoning about conformance must filter these out. Separately, 8 of 17 hyperedges in the snapshot were image-scene noise; the most valuable were command_definition_workflow, fork_release_pipeline and fork_issue_routing, the last two encoding the fork's entire delta.

nodes.label: Extension-Scattering Pattern (Subsystem Verbs on Tree Nouns)
nodes.rationale: Subsystems graft their verbs onto tree nouns via Swift extensions distributed across files: extension TreeNode in 6 files, Window in 7, TilingContainer in 5, and -- per the 2026-08-20 errata -- Workspace in 5, not the 6 originally stated (a loose grep returns 7 only because it also matches the unrelated 'extension WorkspaceCmdArgs'). Dependency direction stays subsystem->tree, keeping the tree types free of subsystem knowledge at the cost of class bodies that no single file contains.
nodes.norm_label: extension-scattering pattern (subsystem verbs on tree nouns)

nodes.label: Three-Tier Behavior Organization
nodes.rationale: AeroSpace organizes behavior in three distinct tiers rather than one uniform scheme: (1) flat conformance tables at the CLI boundary -- 45 CmdArgs conformers and 44 Command conformers wired by two manifest switches; (2) a single inheritance hierarchy for the window tree -- TreeNode plus 10 subclasses; (3) extension-scattering, where subsystems graft verbs onto tree nouns. The tier choice tracks the axis of variation: the CLI varies by command, the tree varies by node kind, and subsystems vary by concern.

nodes.label: Hyperedge ID Collision (fixed by uniquify pass)
nodes.rationale: FIXED per the 2026-08-20 errata. Two distinct hyperedges once shared the id fork_release_pipeline (one from release-adrianlsy.yml, one from fork-maintenance.md), so any consumer keying by id silently dropped one. The committed graph now carries 20 hyperedges with 20 distinct ids, the two fork-release groups being fork_release_pipeline and fork_release_pipeline_docs, and a uniquify pass in the graphify skill prevents recurrence.
